title: Second Helping
logline: At an east-coast wedding reception, hosts keep piling food onto plates, guests protest and then accept, and one man goes back for a third helping without being asked.
human_question: Where does hospitality end and appetite begin, and does it matter?

premise.story: A wedding reception's buffet hour: hosts urging guests to eat more, guests giving in or asking for extra unprompted, and the pride and exhaustion of a family that has been cooking for days.
premise.place: A reception hall or a family's own courtyard set up for a wedding feast, on the east coast.
premise.experience: Noise, heat, plates piled high, and the push and pull between generosity given and appetite taken.

concept_links.why: The concept's own example is eating with relish, arising both spontaneously and through a host's urging; the reception shows both at once, in the same room, at the same meal [C006-M:L7] [C006-M:L9].

The pleasure of a good meal sits among the concept's pleasant-feeling minds, while the sheer scale of a wedding buffet can also tip into the concept's account of pleasant feeling that turns uncomfortable once it is too much [C032-P:L54-L63] [C032-P:L117].

what_camera_could_observe: A guest protesting and then accepting
The last plates cleared at the end of the night
what_must_be_real: A real wedding, a real family's hospitality and their guests' own behaviour. Nothing staged for the buffet scene.

possible_arc.opening: A hall filling with guests and the smell of a feast.
possible_arc.turn: A host's insistence meets a guest's resistance, again and again.
possible_arc.ending_open: The feast winds down, plates emptied or food left over. Reality decides.

requirements: A wedding family willing to have their reception filmed
Guests willing to be filmed eating and being urged to eat
A kitchen willing to be filmed before and after the feast

suggestions.name: A wedding reception hall in Batticaloa or Trincomalee
suggestions.why: Both are established towns with active wedding-reception venues and strong hospitality traditions.
suggestions.verify: No family has been contacted; this is a plausible setting, not a confirmed location.

risks: Sri Lankan hospitality shown without the respect it deserves
A family's private celebration used only for spectacle
drop_if: No family will allow their reception to be filmed with this level of access

connections.note: Two tables: one of habitual daily appetite, one of festive urging to eat more.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
